items.proposed_content: The secure structural comparison is that individual Epstein zeta functions have a real-zero transition reported in a narrow interval around the same leading constant that appears as the exact threshold for their x-average, the Eisenstein constant term. Averaging changes the object from an x-dependent family to its constant Fourier mode, but the source gives no reason why the constant is shared or why the averaged threshold is exact.

items.proposed_content: The two proofs assign their burdens differently: Theorem 2 is summarized as blockwise inequalities in a Hadamard product under reality and functional-equation symmetries, while Theorem 3 invokes Maass-Selberg for modified RH and then separate inequalities for real zeros. The polynomially weighted alternative is only an announced, numerically assisted extension, and its weaker output is confinement and uniform boundedness of finitely many exceptions rather than full RH.

items.proposed_content: The proof separates two kinds of off-line behavior before recombining them. Maass-Selberg positivity confines every nonreal zero to the critical line, while positivity of the Eisenstein average and reflection symmetry confine possible real zeros to (0,1). After pole clearing and antisymmetrization, the remaining right-half real-zero equation becomes the positive scalar level set F(y,sigma)=1. Its derivative at the symmetry point selects y*=4*pi*e^{-gamma}; strict increase of -f'/f then forces either monotone descent with no further crossing for y<=y*, or one rise-and-fall profile with exactly one right-half crossing for y>y*, whose reflection supplies the exceptional pair.

items.proposed_content: Rankwise minimal covolumes are compressed into a canonical polygon whose straightness defines semistability; in rank two, quotienting basis, rotation, and scale choices turns that abstract condition into the explicit modular-region cutoff D_ss. Weng's determinant-one semistable-lattice Mellin integral then becomes the Eisenstein integral over D_ss, and the fundamental-domain partition with D^1 plus Zagier's vanishing identity identifies it with -I(1,s), placing the rank-two zeta function inside Theorem 2's T=1 line-zero case.

items.proposed_content: For the truncation integral, pole clearing exposes critical-line values as a nonvanishing xi amplitude times sin(theta(2t)+t log T), so zeros become crossings of one real phase. The T=1 base case obtains simplicity from a cited differenced-xi theorem; for T>1, adding log T to the nonnegative base phase derivative makes crossings transverse, lets endpoint phase growth yield the xi zero count plus the linear log(T) correction, and makes each fixed crossing occur at lower ordinate as T grows. Attempting the same transfer to a0 introduces the oppositely rotating factor -1+2it, which identifies precisely why the monotonicity proof no longer closes.

items.proposed_content: Horizontal integration over the truncation region instantiates the measure interface by annihilating every nonconstant Fourier mode and retaining the exceptional constant mode, so I(T,s) becomes a two-term T-weighted combination of reflected completed-zeta values. Theorem 4 then supplies strict off-line modulus separation for appropriately shifted entire functions; after scaling xi, rewriting by its functional equation, and clearing the poles of I, the factor T^{2Re(s)-1} preserves and amplifies the right-half-plane inequality when T>=1, while antisymmetry reflects the exclusion to the other half-plane.
